title: Canonical identity compact-support normalization
statement: Fix the coefficient and geometric point setting of [def-pod-conventions] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]: $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. Use compact support at finite level [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and at the other stages [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. There is a specified natural isomorphism $v_\Lambda:R\operatorname{id}_{s!}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ on $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. At finite level it is the termwise identity for the compactification $(\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id})$. Integrally $v_{\mathcal O_E}$ is the inverse of the actual unit $u_C:C\to\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_sC$ of the reduction/total-limit adjunction [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], with $R\operatorname{id}_{s!}C=\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_sC$. Here $\mathcal R_s$ is derived reduction to the strict coefficient tower and $\mathcal L_s$ its total derived inverse limit. This unit is invertible on the derived-complete constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete]. Its inverse is compatible with integral coefficient extension through the canonical completed comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Consequently $v_{\mathcal O_E}$ induces $v_E$ by rationalization and $v_{\Qlb}$ on common finite coefficient-field stages. These are natural for the localized and common-stage morphisms, respectively.

proof.text: For $(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s)$ every site object factors through the open, so extension by zero is the original sheaf and direct image acts identically on complexes. A resolution comparison becomes the identity in the derived category. Set $v_{A_{E,n}}=1$; identities commute with morphisms and coefficient quotients.

proof.text: Apply the strict compact-support tower theorem at $f=\operatorname{id}_s$. The identity operations of step 1 identify its simultaneous quotient tower, including its maps and transitions, with the underlying reduction system. Taking its total limit in the integral definition gives $R\operatorname{id}_{s!,\mathcal O_E}=H_E=\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_s$.

proof.text: At $W=s$ the strict quotient unit-model theorem identifies the actual $u_C$ with $(0,c)$ in that tower's Roos cone, naturally and independently of resolutions. Reconstruction calculus makes $u_C$ invertible on complete $C$. All objects of $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ are complete; put $v_{\mathcal O_E}=u^{-1}$. Its inverse equations keep $H_EC$ in that full category and give naturality.

proof.text: The finite-free comparison supplies $\chi$ and completeness after ordinary scalar extension. The new quotient-comparison lemma identifies the actual scalar maps with completion exchange and its $\chi$ conjugate, using the exchange equation for the units. Thus $v_{\mathcal O_L,\widehat TC}\beta_{L/E,C}=\widehat T(v_{\mathcal O_E,C})$ for the specified completed comparison.

Its associator equation and common-field Hom formula identify the stagewise compact-support operation with the functor on pairs, and give $v_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell,(E,C)}=[E,v_{E,C}]$ with inverse $[E,u_{E,C}]$, natural for all common-stage morphisms.
